title: Fire Storage Volume
applicability: Q_fire from ISO Fire Suppression Rating Schedule or local fire code. Typical residential: 1000–3000 gpm for 2–4 hours. Commercial: 3000–8000 gpm for 4–8 hours. Example: 3000 gpm × 3 hr × 60 = 540,000 gal.
source: ISO FSRS, AWWA M31, local fire codes

title: Equalization Storage (Mass Balance Method)
equation: V_eq = max[Σ(Q_supply - Q_demand) × Δt] - min[Σ(Q_supply - Q_demand) × Δt]

Q_supply.description: Supply rate to tank (constant or scheduled)

applicability: Plot cumulative supply and cumulative demand over 24 hours. Maximum vertical distance between curves = required equalization volume. Rule of thumb: 25% of max day demand. More accurate with actual demand data.
source: General water system engineering, AWWA M32

title: Total Storage Volume
applicability: Some utilities allow partial overlap of fire and equalization storage (fire is short duration, equalization is cyclical). Dead storage typically 5–10% of total. Emergency storage varies: 12 hr to 3 days of average demand.

title: Tank Turnover Time

T_turnover.description: Time to exchange active tank volume

V_active.description: Active storage volume (total minus dead storage)

applicability: Target: T_turnover ≤ 3–5 days for chlorinated systems. If turnover exceeds 5 days, water quality degradation likely (chlorine residual below 0.2 mg/L). Solutions: reduce tank volume, increase throughflow, add mixing.
source: AWWA M42, EPA guidance on distribution system water quality

title: Elevated Tank — Pressure at Ground Level

P_ground.description: Static pressure at ground level below tank

z_ground.description: Ground elevation at point of interest

applicability: For every meter of elevation difference, pressure increases 9.81 kPa (4.33 psi/10 ft). System design pressure target: 275–550 kPa (40–80 psi) at street level. Minimum: 140 kPa (20 psi) under fire flow conditions.

title: Sloshing Wave Height (Seismic — AWWA D100)

d_s.description: Maximum sloshing wave height above static water level

S_a1.description: Design spectral response acceleration at 1-second period

applicability: Simplified form. Full calculation per AWWA D100 Appendix E. Sloshing wave determines required freeboard and shell height above max operating level. Sloshing periods are typically 3–10 seconds (much longer than impulsive response).

title: Steel Tank Shell Thickness (Hoop Stress)
equation: t_shell = γ_w × h × D / (2 × σ_allow × E_joint) + CA

t_shell.description: Shell plate thickness at depth h

h.description: Depth of water above the point (design liquid level to bottom of course)

σ_allow.description: Allowable stress for tank steel (typically 0.40–0.46 × Fy per AWWA D100)

E_joint.description: Joint efficiency (0.85 for single-butt, 1.0 for double-butt radiographed)

CA.description: Corrosion allowance (typically 1.5 mm for interior per AWWA D100)

applicability: Shell courses are thicker at the bottom (higher hydrostatic pressure) and thinner at the top. AWWA D100 specifies minimum thickness of 4.76 mm (3/16 in). Each course designed for the hydrostatic pressure at its bottom.

title: Ring Wall Foundation — Bearing Pressure
equation: q = (W_shell + W_roof + W_water) / (π × D × b_ring) + M_seismic / S_ring

q.description: Maximum bearing pressure under ring wall

W_shell.description: Weight of tank shell per unit circumference

W_roof.description: Weight of roof structure per unit circumference

W_water.description: Weight of water per unit circumference

S_ring.description: Section modulus of ring foundation = π/4 × D² × b_ring

applicability: For flat-bottom welded steel tanks. Ring wall supports shell and transfers loads to foundation soil. Bearing pressure must not exceed allowable soil bearing capacity. Seismic overturning adds non-uniform pressure distribution.
